steps.text: Why study volcanoes?
Because, I hope to play a guitar at the highest spot on Siesta one day. It doesn't have to be at the Obsidian Festival, and preferably at the top of a volcano.
'Volcano Sonatas', that's what I'm planning to call my first album.
I can't wake the volcano up? Ahaha... maybe I should call it 'Volcano Lullabies' instead.
Volcanoes sleep like a log, so I don't think you'll be able to wake it up that easily.
Have you heard of this, about a kind of stone you can find on a volcano?
When the wind blows it away, it makes a sound like beans falling into a bowl.
And if you soak it in water, bubbles fizz like a complex drumline.
Of course it's real. If I find such a stone on a volcano, I'll bring one back to show it to you.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: The doctor's been here. How are you feeling today?
An old man lies on the hospital bed, his head tilted sideways as he looks out the window.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Not so bad, if you hadn't come here to specifically remind me that I'm stuck in bed this summer. And a hospital bed should be more comfortable than an office chair.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Thanks for sparing the energy to tease me, but my butt hasn't known the touch of a chair for the past few days.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Perhaps we should switch places.
The old man turns to look at his grandson standing beside the bed.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: So, my boy, why have you come to see me today?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: There's a letter of intent for relocation, that I hope you can sign.
The city hall staffer whispers the words, as if admitting a mistake.
A tired and bitter silence follows.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: It seems like this renovation plan is just so urgent that it can't even wait until I kick the bucket, huh?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: That's not it...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I just thought you should know about it. Of course, I'd rather get your consent.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: If you want to convince me, you should have at least brought Tysha along to visit.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: She's at work right now...

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Everything you do is to make a living, right? I really don't get why a girl like that would marry a boring man like you.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Let's just say I've inherited your talent for making girls happy.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Hmph...
The hospital ward is quiet, except for the faint sound of fruit being peeled.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Work must have been tough these last few days.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: I've been having nothing but bizarre dreams lately. But after some thinking, I figured I haven't offended anyone, so my guess is that you've been chewed out by a whole lot of people.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Clever old man, you know my job so well.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Well, what's your take? Are you really willing to let this shopping street get demolished, and see the last traces of Old Siesta disappear?

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Costa, there's a guitar in the cabinet behind you. Take it out and play a song for me.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: No thanks... you know that won't work...
The old man speaks no more, and turns his head away toward the window.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I know that Mockingbird Café has been in Siesta longer than the city hall. Many of the shops on that street chose to stay when we moved from the volcano.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: But there are too many factors at play that make our life difficult, and the volcano doesn't even make the list.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Coffee and music can only keep people alive at certain times. If I hadn't lucked out and gotten this job at city hall, your medical bills would be too big a burden on the family.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I'm not complaining, it's just—

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Alright, hand me a pen.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: You're such a brat, Costa. I hate that about you.

steps.name: Tired Voice
steps.text: Maybe I should have tossed you into the sea back when you were mixing your drip coffee with sparkling water.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Thank you very much for not doing that... I do like that about you.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: You want to rent my hotel?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And make a little modification to the hot springs, with your permission of course—price is negotiable.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: I'm not interested in money. It's all the same, not a shred of beauty!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Well, money isn't the only bargaining chip. I definitely have something here that you'll be very interested in.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Like this, for example?

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: This photo... is that a piece of exhibit-grade obsidian?!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: So how about renting these few hot spring hotels of yours to me for a few days, and I'll move this piece of obsidian over?

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Don't play around with me, this is from some private museum's precious collection, how could you—

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: Wait, you...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Uh-huh.

steps.name: Pelipper
steps.text: You'll keep your word?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Words hold no proof, so let's sign a contract, shall we?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Snowsant, can you do some research to check if my plan is feasible?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: It's probably... doable...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Good, that means it is! I'll trust your judgement.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: No, no, no...! I'm not certain, I'll need some tools and materials... and a bit of... no, a lot of time!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Ga yau! I'll move on to the next step.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Since we've decided to focus on making the residents of this street welcome our redevelopment, we'll have to make sure it's perfect.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: We can't waste this chance, with all the tourists drawn in by Bison's ads for his trade fair...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (No, not here...)

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ('Data Model for Volcanic Eruptions' is definitely not in the files Professor Magna left for Adele.)

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (But why does Keller have this notebook with her...?)

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Good work today. Cup of coffee?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Ah, no thanks, I'm not a coffee person... is Adele here today?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Today isn't a work day, so what are you doing here?

spans.text: Today isn't a work day, so what are

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Do you need these old documents for your work over at city hall?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Keller, why on Terra did you invite Adele here?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I believe I made it quite clear before. The research in this museum is related to the Naumanns, and the imminent eruption of Siesta's volcano is a rare observation opportunity.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Adele is their child, and also an excellent volcanologist, so it is only right I extend an invitation to her.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Only now, after so many years with zero contact?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: You didn't attend the Naumanns' funeral after the incident at Mount Unna. You vanished without a trace from academic circles, and stopped your teaching work at the school a year ago.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Just what have you been up to these last few years? What are you running from?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: As you can see, the only thing I've done these past few years is organize all the volcanic research materials that now sit in this very museum.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Kahn, everyone has their limits. I no longer have any energy to do volcano field work. I'm preparing to retire after the museum is finished, and I've observed Mount Siesta's eruption.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: What... retire? Why would you even consider 'retirement' at all?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: The Naumanns left all their unpublished research data to you and Adele, enough to make your mark on the academic world, and yet now you're saying you want to retire?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Or could it be that you've already placed a price tag on that data behind closed doors and gained something even better in exchange?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Kahn, I don't know what you're—

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller, are you in here?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ...Keller.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Whatever your plans, I hope you'll consider the Naumanns before making any decisions.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Adele is their only child, and the only hope they've left behind. She's already contracted Oripathy, and her condition isn't the best either...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: ...I just hope she can be happy and free.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: ...I'm in here, Adele. Come in!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller, I found the exhibit, and already put it back in the display cabinet.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Alright... good work.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor, what's wrong?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: ...Nothing much.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Where did you find the exhibit?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It was with a beckbeast that sneaked into the museum...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: How strange...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Alright, if there's nothing else, you can—

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller, there's something else I wanted to mention! I met a shopkeeper on the street, and he asked me to return this book to you.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: A shopkeeper in the commercial street?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Bang!

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I can taste the fatigue in the air, so painfully bitter and sickeningly sour. Just who is it coming from?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly! You scared me... why are you here?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I just saw a beautiful streak of blue across the city. Want to go to a hot spring?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly, I still have some research to do...

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: No, no, no. 'Research', such a bitter word it makes you all wrinkly. The volcano is right there, and the material won't disappear either, so you can always come back to continue your research anytime, but—
Dolly lightly tips his toes and spins in mid-air, in what looks to be a somewhat comical dance.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Some things are so fleeting that you'll never get a second chance to see if you miss it.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: For example—

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Eyja—finally found you!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Let's go. Want to visit the hot springs together?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hot springs?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I don't have the ability to control people's hearts, by the way.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: But what? Didn't bring a swimsuit? That's fine, I have some over there!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Besides us two, Snowsant will be there too, and we'll also call Ceylon in a bit. I even bought some of the latest facial cream—they say there's volcanic ash inside.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Plus, I have an important thing to ask of you, and you're the only one who can do it!

steps.name: Tourist A
steps.text: Is this... the latest record player on the Columbian market? I didn't think I would be able to see one in Siesta...! I've been paying close attention, they only started selling these just a few days ago!

steps.name: Tourist B
steps.text: But these are the leftover stock, you already missed the first wave...

steps.name: Tourist B
steps.text: You don't know this, but there was a super long line here this morning. The limited editions with Emperor's signature even come with a copy of his latest album, and that sold out forever ago!

steps.name: Tourist A
steps.text: EMPEROR'S LATEST ALBUM?! Isn't that dropping next week? Is this what they call an early access batch? Who could even pull this off?!

steps.name: Tourist C
steps.text: It's not just Emperor's album either! There's also signed copies of Miss Sora's album, a Kazimierzian Radiant Knight helmet model replica, and 'Czerny's Klavier Kollektion'! ...Wait, what's this?

steps.name: Tourist B
steps.text: Huh, to think I'd find one of our Sargonian Crabbie Pumpies here... but what use does it even have here in Siesta?

steps.name: Tourist C
steps.text: Who cares, it's cute and that's all that matters! Did you miss the line of people queueing up to buy them?

steps.name: Tourist B
steps.text: Whoa, they even got dates here!

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Dates?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Excuse me, Mr. Sargonian.
Byrd casually strums a Sargon style ditty.

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Can you tell me a story of plucking dates in the hot and dry breeze?

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: This are instruments imported from Leithanien, and I have to say, those Leithanians sure are stellar at any music-related stuff. You can try if you like, and if you don't know how to play one, I can teach you a little too!

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: The piece I just played? I performed it when me and my wife confessed our feelings to each other, hehe. If you fancy learning it, I have a sheet here that you can have!

steps.name: Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: The best snacks around here, you ask? See that bearded old man on the left? His ice cream is the best!

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Slowly now, take it easy. Strawberry for you, orange for you, yours is coffee, and what else? Coconut with chocolate? Oww... No need to rush, we have plenty here...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Mister, give me a tea flavored one.

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Sure, coming right up!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I'll send this to Schwarz too... it'll will make her drool.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Dr. Ceylon! You here for the trade fair too?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Stopped by for a stroll since I happened to have some time today.

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Enis, you good lad! Thanks again for fixing the cash register this morning, things would've been so hectic otherwise.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It's nothing, just helping out is all! How's business?

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: So good I almost thought I was back in the old Siesta.

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: But why haven't I seen that Costa fellow anywhere today? He spent the whole day running all over the place for this, and now that everything is in motion, that man is nowhere to be found.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Maybe there's other work to do at city hall today...

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: That rascal. Doesn't even know how to ditch work...

steps.name: Tourist A
steps.text: Boss, gimme a cone!

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Coming!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Feel free to come try our cocktails over at the White Volcano too!

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: ...You brat!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Haha!
Enis leans against the soda fountain, watching the surrounding people come and go.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Did you see my little siblings earlier?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: It's their first time in such a bustling place. They kept clamoring for some volcano coffee or something on our way here, but as soon as I handed them a little pocket money, they were gone in a flash.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Pfft.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Though, I don't think I've spotted any kids here...

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: The little runts aren't here. If you want to find them, you have to over to east street!

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: They say there's a new amusement park over there or something, and my own brat even told me over breakfast he'd help me look after the store. Hmph, I haven't heard from him ever since he learned about the place!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: An amusement park?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Can I open my eyes now, Miss Swire? Also, what was the important thing you were mentioning earlier?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Did some of those secretly mined obsidian appear in this hotel too? Or do you need a nominal volcanologist for your work? Or...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Neither!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No volcanoes here, and no data either. Only a comforting hot spring, so now you just have to get into some pretty clothes, and then—

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Alright, you can open your eyes now!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Wow... there's so many tourists!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What happened here? Wasn't it just a hot spring before?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It's so lively, just like Siesta a few years back...
A few tourists erupt into cheering, and Adele recovers from her surprise.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: There's so many kayaks and water installations here, Miss Swire, are these your...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Yup, this is the waterpark I'm setting up for the commercial street!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Wow... did you do all of this by yourself?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Not by myself, of course. I provided the plans, but we have our Chief Genius Engineer from Lungmen to thank for making this a reality, Snowsant!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Um! Miss, Miss Swire... that title is a bit too much...!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Hmm~? Really now?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Yan's number one, Terra's number one Genius Engineer?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ahhh—!!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Wait, Snowsant! Don't run around like that, be careful!

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: Ohhhh—!!

steps.name: Surprised Tourist Scream
steps.text: It—It's flying—!!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: How did you do that? How are these surf kayaks actually flying straight from one hot spring channel to the other?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Um, actually, it's not as complicated as it looks, we just needed to add a pneumatic ejection device on the waterways, so once the kayak reaches this spot, it'll trigger the mechanism, and then it'll—

steps.name: Surprised Tourist Scream
steps.text: Yay! I can fly!

steps.name: Surprised Tourist Scream
steps.text: Mama——!!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Um, there aren't any guardrails on the waterways, so I'm a little worried about—

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I redesigned the kayaks according to Swire's plan, and they come equipped with a comprehensive emergency cushioning system.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: It's also the second way you can play with these, as bumper kayaks! They can freely collide on the waterways, and the cushioning system will absorb all the impact force, using it to power the kayaks' water guns that spray water forward.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I didn't mention it to the tourists, but many of them seem to have already mastered this secret.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Look, over there—

steps.name: Little Tourist Exclaiming
steps.text: Ah—Ahh—!
Along with a shriek, a kayak spins in the waterway, seemingly about to fall off the channel.
The airbags at the kayak's edge quickly inflate, wrapping up the passengers. But as the kayak drops, its trajectory is interrupted suddenly, as if there is a transparent barrier in the air.
Water splashes onto the ground, the completely wrapped kayak sways and falls downward.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Hey—! You alright? Anyone hurt?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I'll go take a look first, Eyja. Just wait here a second!
Tourists surround the fallen kayak, but there is only giggling bubbling from the center.
With a puff of the bulging air cushions, two children emerge from within.

steps.name: Unhappy Girl
steps.text: Hmph! It's all your fault for moving around so much!

steps.name: Unhappy Girl
steps.text: We didn't catch the little lamb, and our 'Siestan Adventure' is ruined!

steps.name: Very Happy Boy
steps.text: Nuh-uh, it's not my fault the lamb ran so fast!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Lamb?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I don't see them here either... it must be tiring taking care of your younger siblings, yes? Children of that age love to play around and make so much noise.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: *sigh* Thanks for the concern, but it's fine this way too. They're having fun at least.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You have a lot to worry about, as an older brother.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Now that I think back on some past incidents... pfft. I think like a friend might feel the same sometimes.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Do you have an older sibling, Dr. Ceylon? I've never heard—

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: It's your fault! All your fault!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Hey! You brats! Where did you run off to?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Enis!

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: It's Enis!

steps.name: Boy & Girl
steps.text: We sat on a big air cushion boat, and chased a fluffy little lamb!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: What are you talking about? What lamb...?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: A fluffy little lamb that lifted our boat up with its head to play with it like a ball!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: When we catch it, we gotta make it sit in our boat!

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Enis, over there! The lamb is back!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Where?

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: Look up!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Wait, these...

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Our surfboards... why are they flying in the sky?!
Surfboards and swim rings.
They use the hot spring steam to leap into the air, jumping over Fashion Street and into the sky, beyond the tourists' view.
Everyone's eyes are glued to the objects swirling around as if living creatures.
And Adele sees something slightly different than the others.
The surfboards cruising across the sky have sheep standing on them.
They don't seem content with just racing the waterways—
Hot water, vapor, colorful surfboards and swim rings. The sheep sweep them all up, and together they pour into the hustle and bustle of Fashion Street.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (This is bad...! Dolly said he would teach them a lesson, was he lying to me?)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: (Oh no, they're splashing the hot spring water everywhere!)

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Snowsant, did you design a flying surfboard behind my back because I rejected your idea for an observation wheel suspended above the hot spring?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Didn't you arrange this, Miss Swire?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No... it wasn't me either.
The two look at each other, and then hesitantly turn their gazes toward Adele, who has been standing to the side the whole time.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Adele...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: No, no, no! It's not me either!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Odd. Could it be Bison then?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Yoohoo—! Little lamb, fluffy little lamb!

steps.name: Boy
steps.text: The lamb is flying!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I'll go look!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Whoa—Eyja, Snowsant!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: The surfboards are really flying! Whatever, let's get on those things!

steps.name: Tourist A
steps.text: Who's in charge here? Quick, someone should mass-produce these surfboards!

steps.name: Tourist B
steps.text: Woohoo!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: *sigh* Mr. Dolly...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Is this the hot spring you were talking about...?
